draft.title: The gold rushes
card: Gold was found in Victoria in 1851. News spread fast, and the colony's population grew very quickly.
Hundreds of thousands of migrants arrived, from Britain, Ireland, Europe, North America and China. Many Chinese miners came from southern China.
The government charged miners a licence fee to dig for gold. Miners had to pay it whether or not they found any gold, and many were angry about it.
In 1854 anger over licences, and over how they were enforced, led miners at Ballarat to build the Eureka Stockade. Troops and police attacked it, and many miners and some soldiers died.
draft.remember: Gold in 1851 brought migrants to Victoria, and anger over licences led to the Eureka Stockade in 1854.

a.q: Why did many miners on the Victorian goldfields become angry with the government in the early 1850s?
opts: They had to pay a licence fee whether or not they found gold
They were banned from digging for gold in Victoria
They were forced to hand over all gold they found
They were not allowed to travel to the goldfields
a.why: Miners paid the licence fee before they knew if they would find any gold, and this caused anger that led to Eureka. Miners were allowed to dig and keep their gold, so the other options are wrong.
a.clue: Think about what miners paid before they dug.

b.q: Li Wei leaves southern China in 1855 and sails to Victoria. What is the most likely reason he goes?
opts: He hopes to find gold after hearing the news of the rushes
He has been sent as a convict by the British government
He is joining the troops that attacked the Eureka Stockade
He has been told to build the new Commonwealth parliament
b.why: The gold rushes drew many migrants, including many from China, who hoped to find gold. Convict transport and the Commonwealth parliament are not linked to this, and the Eureka Stockade was built by miners, not troops.
b.clue: What was found in Victoria in 1851?

a.best: They had to pay a licence fee whether or not they found gold

b.best: He hopes to find gold after hearing the news of the rushes

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and repeats the card's exact phrase 'whether or not they found gold', so a student could pick it by matching words rather than knowing the idea.

Why (b) says 'the Eureka Stockade was built by miners, not troops', but the option is about joining the troops that attacked it. A clearer reason is that the Stockade was attacked in 1854, before Li Wei left in 1855.

proposal.title: The gold rushes
card: Gold was found in Victoria in 1851. News spread fast, and the colony's population grew very quickly.
Hundreds of thousands of migrants arrived, from Britain, Ireland, Europe, North America and China. Many Chinese miners came from southern China.
The government charged each miner a licence fee to dig for gold. The fee was due before any digging, so miners with empty claims paid the same as lucky ones, and many were angry.
In 1854 anger over licences, and over how they were enforced, led miners at Ballarat to build the Eureka Stockade. Troops and police attacked it, and many miners and some soldiers died.
proposal.remember: Gold in 1851 brought migrants to Victoria, and anger over licences led to the Eureka Stockade in 1854.

a.q: Why did many miners on the Victorian goldfields become angry with the government in the early 1850s?
opts: They paid to dig even when they found no gold
They paid a tax on each ounce of gold they found
They were banned from keeping any gold they found
They had to sell all their gold to the government
a.why: The licence fee was paid to dig, before anyone knew if a claim held gold, so unlucky miners paid as much as lucky ones. A tax on each ounce found is a different kind of charge: it would only fall on miners who found gold.
a.clue: Was the fee linked to digging or to finding?

b.q: Li Wei leaves southern China in 1855 and sails to Victoria. What is the most likely reason he goes?
opts: He hopes to find gold after hearing the news of the rushes
He has been sent as a convict by the British government
He is joining the troops that attacked the Eureka Stockade
He has been told to build the new Commonwealth parliament
b.why: The gold rushes drew many migrants, including many from southern China, who hoped to find gold. The Eureka Stockade was attacked in 1854, before Li Wei left in 1855, and the Commonwealth parliament did not exist yet. China was not a British colony sending convicts.
b.clue: What was found in Victoria in 1851?
